SELECTED_INDEX: 1
CONFIDENCE: 0.27
EXPLANATION: The strong Raman band at 2232 cm⁻¹ identifies an aromatic nitrile (C≡N stretch, rule GFQ-009). Bands typical of an aromatic ring appear at 1587 cm⁻¹ (C=C stretch) and 3073 cm⁻¹ (aromatic C–H stretch).  

The key discriminant is the medium-weak band at 552 cm⁻¹: aryl C–Br stretching vibrations normally fall in the 500–600 cm⁻¹ window, whereas aryl C–F stretches occur near 1000–1350 cm⁻¹. The spectrum indeed shows bands at 1071, 1180 and 1197 cm⁻¹ that fit ring modes but only a single, distinct low-frequency band near 552 cm⁻¹—consistent with one C–Br bond. No broad O–H (3200–3600 cm⁻¹) or N–H (~3300 cm⁻¹, 1600 cm⁻¹ bend) features are present, disfavoring candidates bearing OH or NH₂ groups.  

Among the candidates, only 1 (N#Cc1ccc(Br)cc1) contains a single nitrile and a para-bromophenyl ring, matching both the nitrile stretch and the characteristic C–Br band. Therefore candidate 1 best fits the experimental Raman peaks.
